chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked, 'Is the obligatory charity (zakat) permissible for the Banu Hashim?' He replied, 'That is the obligatory charity due upon the people; it is not permissible for us. As for other types, there is no harm in it. And if it were so (that all charity was forbidden to us), they would not have been able to go to Mecca, for most of its water is charity (sadaqa).'.
ai.seo_question: Is zakat permissible for Banu Hashim?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between *zakat* (obligatory alms-tax) and *sadaqa* (general charity), ruling that the former is prohibited for Banu Hashim while the latter is permissible. He illustrates this by citing the waters of Mecca as *sadaqa*; if they were classified as *zakat*, the Banu Hashim would be barred from using them, thereby highlighting the practical distinction in resource utilization for the Prophet's clan.
